Local NHS Healthcare Trusts providing mental health services, crisis response, and youth wellbeing support.

supported_services_and_partners.contact: Call 111 for 24/7 NHS mental health support

supported_services_and_partners.description: Local community trusts and family support hubs offering guidance for parents, carers, and young people.
Confidential support services helping young people and families with addiction recovery, smoking cessation, and substance awareness.
Surrey's free healthy lifestyles service, available to people who live, work or are registered with a GP in Surrey. Self-refer via the One You Surrey website.
services_offered: Stop Smoking Programme: 12 weeks of free support including nicotine replacement therapy and weekly appointments with a stop smoking advisor, via face-to-face clinics or telephone. Eligibility: currently using tobacco products, aged 12 or over, living, working or registered with a GP in Surrey.

Adult Weight Management: 12 weeks of free support through Gloji programmes, Slimming World or Man v Fat. Eligibility: aged 18 or over, BMI over 30 (over 27.5 for South Asian, black and minority ethnic groups), living, working or registered with a GP in Surrey.
Gloji Option 1: digital only — 24/7 access to expert videos, workouts, meal ideas and more.
Gloji Option 2: digital plus group support — group sessions held at Guildford Spectrum in 12-week blocks.
Gloji Option 3: digital plus 1:1 support — one-to-one calls with a personal health mentor.
Slimming World Voucher: 12-week access to a local Slimming World group.

Man v Fat: for men aged 18+ with a starting BMI of 27.5 or higher who live, work or are registered with a GP in Surrey. Tailored digital support plus weekly sessions with a weigh-in followed by a 30-minute game of football, at Kings College (Park Barn Drive, Guildford) and Woking Sportsbox (Egley Road).
supported_services_and_partners.how_to_refer: Individuals can self-refer via the One You Surrey website.

faqs.question: Where can I get mental health support at the event?
faqs.answer: You can visit the dedicated 'Mental Wellbeing & Mindfulness' zone where partners like Sport in Mind, NHS wellbeing stalls, and local support hubs offer free guidance and resources.

faqs.question: Are there services available for family care, smoking, or drug support?
faqs.answer: Yes! The event exhibition zone features community support stalls providing confidential advice on family mentoring, smoking cessation, and substance recovery guidance.

faqs.question: What should I do if I need urgent mental health help?
faqs.answer: For immediate crisis support, speak to an on-site welfare staff member or contact NHS 111 (Option 2) for 24/7 mental health crisis services.
